title: RTI: Asking Your Government

endcard.line: Pictures: The National Archives UK (CC BY 3.0); Ankur Panchbudhe from Pune, India (CC BY 2.0)

anim.below: to answer a request for information

segments.say: Ask a government office for information, and it must reply within thirty days. That promise comes from the Right to Information Act.
Parliament passed the Act in June two thousand five. Its aim is transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority.

anim.title: How a request moves
items: You write to the Public Information Officer
Within 30 days: the information, or reasons for refusal

segments.say: You write to the office's Public Information Officer and pay the prescribed fee. Within thirty days, the officer must give the information, or refuse it for a reason the Act allows.
If the information concerns someone's life or liberty, the deadline is forty-eight hours.
People below the poverty line pay no fee. And if the office misses the deadline, the information must be given free.

anim.title: If the answer isn't good enough
items: Second appeal: Central or State Information Commission

segments.say: If you are not satisfied, you can appeal. A second appeal goes to the Central or a State Information Commission, within ninety days.
For GS Two, remember the numbers: thirty days, forty-eight hours, and an Act from two thousand five that made information a citizen's right.

sources: Right to Information Act, 2005 (Act 22 of 2005), official text on cic.gov.in: enacted 15 June 2005; preamble on transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority; s.7(1) reply within thirty days, forty-eight hours where information concerns the life or liberty of a person; s.7(5) no fee from persons below the poverty line; s.7(6) information free of charge where time limits are not met; s.19(3) second appeal within ninety days to the Central or State Information Commission

quiz.q: Within how long must information be given if it concerns a person's life or liberty?
What happens if a public authority misses the RTI deadline?
options: The information must be given free of charge
quiz.why: s.7(6): free of charge where time limits are not met.

quiz.q: A second appeal under the RTI Act goes to…
quiz.why: s.19(3): the Central or State Information Commission, within ninety days.

reviewNote: All facts are from the Act's official text. The script doesn't give the fee amount (it is set by rules, not the Act) or the first-appeal officer's details. The files photo is from the UK National Archives (a generic shelf view); swap it for an Indian office photo if one is cleared. Moving facts: the 2019 amendment on Information Commissioners' terms isn't covered here.
